name: ROCM_PATH
recommended: Set to the exact unpacked SDK root for a tarball install.
risk: A stale value can mix release lines.

name: PATH
recommended: Prepend or append one ROCm SDK bin directory consistently.
risk: Multiple hipconfig binaries can select the wrong SDK.

name: LD_LIBRARY_PATH
recommended: Use only for nonstandard/tarball installs; prefer a container or ldconfig file for deployment.
risk: Can silently load libraries from the wrong release line.

name: HIPCXX
recommended: Resolve from the active ROCm SDK.
risk: Do not point it to a system Clang from another generation.

name: HIP_PATH
recommended: Resolve from active hipconfig.
scope: HIP CMake package and runtime discovery
risk: Mismatch with HIPCXX creates a mixed toolchain.

name: CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES
recommended: Set gfx1151 explicitly for a single-target Strix Halo build.
risk: Omitting it can produce a larger or wrong-target build; requires CMake >=3.21.

name: GPU_TARGETS
recommended: Use only for projects/ROCm packages that consume it; direct CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES is clearer in current llama.cpp.
risk: Project-specific behavior.

name: AMDGPU_TARGETS
recommended: Prefer CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES for current CMake projects.
risk: Can be ignored or translated depending on project version.

name: CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER_ROCM_ROOT
recommended: Set only when a nonstandard SDK layout cannot be auto-discovered.
risk: Can hide an inconsistent install if used reflexively.

name: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES
recommended: Use for deterministic single-GPU selection.
risk: Device numbering can differ from other APIs.

name: ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
recommended: Use when HSA-level filtering is required; avoid contradictory visibility variables.
risk: Contradictory HIP and ROCR filters can confuse diagnostics.

name: HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
recommended: Set to 1 only to localize an asynchronous fault.
risk: Severely changes timing and performance.

name: TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL
recommended: Set to 1 only for the AMD ROCm 7.2.1 PyTorch recipe that documents it; it is not a llama.cpp, HIP, or system-wide requirement.
risk: Experimental application behavior; irrelevant to llama.cpp and may change across PyTorch/ROCm release lines.

name: HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION
recommended: Leave unset on a native current gfx1151 stack. The ROCmFPX fork documents 11.5.1 for its own HIP path.
risk: 11.0.0/11.0.3 spoofing did not fix old-stack failures and can select incompatible code paths.

name: GGML_HIP_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY
recommended: Use only with the pinned ROCmFPX fork recipe that documents it.
risk: Not an upstream llama.cpp compatibility requirement.

name: VK_DRIVER_FILES
recommended: Set only to force a verified ICD manifest during controlled A/B tests.
risk: A wrong path makes Vulkan devices disappear; ignored in elevated contexts.

name: VK_ICD_FILENAMES
recommended: Use VK_DRIVER_FILES instead for new recipes.
risk: Stale shell configuration can force AMDVLK or a nonexistent driver unexpectedly.

name: VK_LOADER_DEBUG
recommended: Use all for a one-shot loader trace.
risk: Verbose; may expose filesystem paths in logs.

name: GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS
recommended: Not a gfx1151 default; use only when investigating graph-related faults and record the result.
risk: May reduce performance and is sourced from a related RDNA4 report.

name: HSA_ENABLE_SDMA
recommended: Leave enabled on a validated current stack. Set to 0 only for a bounded A/B test or the cited kernel 6.19.x community setup; remove it after diagnosis unless independently reproduced.
example: HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0 ./reproducer  # diagnostic or cited 6.19.x setup only
risk: Changes transfer paths and performance; can conceal rather than repair a kernel, firmware, or runtime mismatch.

name: amdgpu.cwsr_enable
recommended: Leave default on current supported stacks; use =0 only to contain the documented legacy ROCm 7.1/MES issue while migrating.
risk: Disables a kernel feature and can mask an obsolete stack.

name: amd_iommu
recommended: Do not disable IOMMU by default when USB4, virtualization, device isolation, or RDMA security matters; benchmark in your threat model.
risk: Disabling IOMMU weakens DMA isolation and may conflict with USB4/RDMA security requirements.
